topics.name: Reference Closure
topics.purpose: Group deterministic recursive reference resolution across the active canonical graph.

metadata.finite_traversal_rule: Visited identity/reference pairs prevent infinite traversal while preserving explicit cycle observations.

semantics.closure_definition: The active canonical graph is reference-closed when every machine-significant reference reachable from an active root resolves exactly once to an eligible canonical target or is explicitly represented as a permitted external/unresolved boundary defined by its owning contract.
semantics.resolution_rule: Reference resolution uses canonical identity plus explicit active/source-role semantics. It does not use filenames, directory paths, nearest-name matching, latest-version heuristics or Topic proximity.
semantics.dimension_preservation_rule: Resolving a ref never erases why that ref exists. containment refs remain containment; Topic refs remain Topic refs; authority refs remain authority; causal refs remain causal.

cycle_rule.general: A cycle is not automatically invalid.
cycle_rule.allowed: Cycles are allowed where the owning semantic dimension explicitly permits recursive graphs.
cycle_rule.forbidden: A cycle is invalid where the owning contract declares acyclicity, such as prohibited Topic inheritance/composition cycles or another explicitly acyclic dimension.
cycle_rule.reader_behavior: Record the cycle and validate it against the owning semantic dimension; never break it silently.

semantics.external_boundary_rule: External references are not treated as resolved internal canonical identities unless the owning contract explicitly defines that external reference form and its resolution semantics.
semantics.closure_vs_traceability: Reference closure answers whether every explicit ref resolves. Bidirectional traceability answers whether meaningful higher/lower-level traversal can be reconstructed with provenance. Both are required and neither substitutes for the other.

invariants.rule: Every required active internal reference resolves exactly once.
Reference resolution preserves the semantic dimension and source provenance of the reference.
Closure traversal does not mutate canonical semantics.

hard_gates.condition: A required active internal reference resolves to no eligible target.
A required active reference resolves to more than one eligible target.
Reference resolution requires filename, directory path or physical proximity.
Reference resolution uses fuzzy/nearest naming instead of exact canonical identity semantics.
Reference normalization or traversal loses whether the reference represented Topic, structure, authority, dependency, causality or another explicit dimension.
A cycle forbidden by its owning semantic dimension is silently ignored or broken by traversal.
A reference to historical, superseded or otherwise inactive material is silently treated as an active semantic target without an explicit historical reference role.

references.purpose: Determines whether a candidate target participates in the active semantic graph.
Reference closure supplies resolved graph edges used by bidirectional traces.
Dangling or ambiguous active references become explicit semantic gaps.

prose.summary: Defines exact recursive reference closure for the active canonical graph while preserving the type, provenance and semantic dimension of every reference.
notes: Unlocked until repository-wide 1.4 validation proves closure from Master through every active canonical root.
